facts.statement: The genus Caupedactylus was first named and described by Alexander Wilhelm Armin Kellner in 2013.
facts.quote: The genus was first named and described by Alexander Wilhelm Armin Kellner in 2013.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen MN 4726-V dates to about 110 million years ago from the Albian stage of the Romualdo Formation in the Araripe basin.
facts.quote: Caupedactylus is known from the holotype specimen MN 4726-V, probably found in the Araripe basin in a layer of the Romualdo Formation dating from the Albian, about 110 million years old.

facts.statement: The fossil specimen was extracted from chalkstone using an acid bath.
facts.quote: The specimen was freed from the chalkstone by an acid bath.

facts.statement: Kellner estimated the wingspan of Caupedactylus at 3.3 meters, making it the largest known tapejarine.
facts.quote: Kellner estimated the wingspan of Caupedactylus at 3.3 m, making it the largest known tapejarine.

facts.statement: The skull of Caupedactylus is approximately forty-six centimeters long.
facts.quote: The skull is about forty-six centimetres long.

facts.statement: The snout features a crest on the premaxilla that extends both forward and backward along the skull.
facts.quote: The snout sports a crest on the premaxilla extending both to the front and to the rear of the skull.

facts.statement: The skull crest is very thin, measuring about half a millimeter at its upper part.
facts.quote: The crest is very thin, about half a millimetre at the upper part.

facts.statement: The ascending branch of the jugal bone connects to the lacrimal bone at a reclining angle of 115 degrees.
facts.quote: The ascending branch of the jugal bone, connecting to the lacrimal bone, is strongly reclining at an angle of 115 degrees.

facts.statement: A 2019 phylogenetic analysis by Kellner and colleagues recovered Caupedactylus as the basalmost tapejarine.
facts.quote: In 2019 however, Kellner (the describer of Caupedactylus) and colleagues had included it in a phylogenetic analysis where it was recovered as the basalmost tapejarine.

facts.statement: Caupedactylus lived between 119.57 and 113.2 million years ago during the Aptian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Aptian (119.57 to 113.2 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Caupedactylus is an extinct genus of tapejarid azhdarchoid pterosaur found in the Early Cretaceous Romualdo Formation of the Araripe Basin in northeastern Brazil.
rejected.quote: Caupedactylus is an extinct genus of tapejarid azhdarchoid pterosaur known from the Early Cretaceous period (Albian stage) of what is now the Romualdo Formation of the Araripe Basin in northeastern Brazil.
